+# --- run registry (§2 generation token) -------------------------------------
+
+def _registry_rows(store: EventLog, run_id: str) -> int:
+    with store.conn.cursor() as cur:
+        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM runs WHERE run_id = %s", (run_id,))
+        return cur.fetchone()[0]
+
+
+def test_first_emit_registers_the_run(make_gateway):
+    """A run carries a generation token from its first event: the write path opens the
+    run when absent, so no run that has ever been emitted into is missing from `runs`
+    (and its restore-time `bump-generation` is therefore never inert)."""
+    gateway, store = make_gateway(run_id="reg-fresh")
+    assert store.generation() is None                         # fresh id: no token yet
+    unwrap(gateway.emit(actor=PLANNER, event_type="goal.received", payload={"text": "g"}))
+    assert store.generation() == 1
+
+
+def test_second_emit_leaves_the_registry_untouched(make_gateway):
+    """Opening is a no-op when present — one row, and no churn on every later emit."""
+    gateway, store = make_gateway(run_id="reg-twice")
+    gateway.emit(actor=PLANNER, event_type="goal.received", payload={"text": "a"})
+    gateway.emit(actor=PLANNER, event_type="goal.received", payload={"text": "b"})
+    assert store.generation() == 1
+    assert _registry_rows(store, "reg-twice") == 1
+
+
+def test_replayed_emit_registers_a_run_that_has_events_but_no_row(make_gateway):
+    """The state the durable run is actually in — events written before the write path
+    opened runs, so no registry row — closes on the NEXT emit whatever kind it is. A
+    replay (the common shape for an at-least-once caller) returns early without folding
+    or gating, so the open has to sit ahead of that early return or the one run this
+    order exists for stays tokenless and its restore-time bump stays inert."""
+    gateway, store = make_gateway(run_id="reg-replay")
+    kw = dict(actor=PLANNER, event_type="goal.received", payload={"text": "g"},
+              idempotency_key="k1")
+    first = unwrap(gateway.emit(**kw))
+    store.conn.execute("DELETE FROM runs WHERE run_id = %s", ("reg-replay",))
+    assert store.generation() is None                          # events, but no token
+    replay = gateway.emit(**kw)
+    assert isinstance(replay, Accepted)
+    assert replay.event.event_id == first.event_id             # still a replay, not a re-append
+    assert store.generation() == 1                             # ...and now registered
+    assert _registry_rows(store, "reg-replay") == 1
+
+
+def test_emit_into_a_registered_run_preserves_its_generation(make_gateway):
+    """Already-registered runs are unchanged — in particular an emit never resets the
+    generation a restore bumped, which would un-invalidate every stale cursor."""
+    gateway, store = make_gateway(run_id="reg-bumped")
+    store.open_run()
+    store.bump_generation()
+    assert store.generation() == 2
+    gateway.emit(actor=PLANNER, event_type="goal.received", payload={"text": "a"})
+    assert store.generation() == 2
+    assert _registry_rows(store, "reg-bumped") == 1
+
+
+def test_refused_emit_registers_the_run_too(make_gateway):
+    """A refusal still lands an event — the gateway.rejected feedback record (§5) — so
+    the run it landed in must carry a token as well."""
+    gateway, store = make_gateway(run_id="reg-refused")
+    res = gateway.emit(actor=COORD, event_type="task.assigned", task_id="t1",
+                       payload={"worker": "w1"})
+    assert isinstance(res, Rejected)
+    assert store.generation() == 1
+
+
+def test_registration_rolls_back_with_a_failed_append(make_gateway):
+    """Opening shares the event insert's transaction: a payload that fails structural
+    validation leaves no event AND no registry row (never a phantom generation)."""
+    gateway, store = make_gateway(run_id="reg-atomic")
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        gateway.emit(actor=WORKER, event_type="task.reported", task_id="t1",
+                     payload={"ref": "not-a-ref", "kind": "finding"})
+    assert store.generation() is None
+    assert store.read_run() == []
+
+

@@ -0,0 +1,190 @@
+# Result — register the durable run (make the generation token real)
+
+**Task:** run-registration · **Order:** `projects/omegahive/orders/2026-07-21-run-registration.md` · **Date:** 2026-07-21
+
+## What shipped
+
+**Code (branch `feature/run-registration` in the omegahive repo, off `main`; four commits):**
+
+- **Idempotent open on the write path** — `src/omegahive/gateway/gateway.py`. `Gateway.emit()`
+  now calls `store.open_run()` (an `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` against `runs`) inside
+  the *same* transaction as the event insert. It is the write path's **first** step — ahead of
+  the idempotency early-return, the advisory lock and the gate — because every one of those
+  exits leaves an event standing in the run: a replay returns an event already committed, a
+  refusal appends a `gateway.rejected`. So a run is registered by any emit that touches it,
+  including the two shapes that write nothing new, and no run that has ever been written to is
+  missing its generation token — `bump-generation` on it is never inert. The replay case is
+  not a corner: a wrapper retrying an at-least-once emit, or an operator re-running the same
+  `hive emit`, derives the same idempotency key and dedups, and that is the likeliest shape of
+  the "next real emit" that wires up the live run. No advisory lock is needed for the open
+  (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` is its own serialisation), so replays keep their fast path: no
+  lock, no fold, no gate.
+- **Tests** (red-green) — `tests/test_write_path.py` gains a run-registry section: first emit
+  registers (`generation` 1); a second emit is a no-op on the registry (one row, still
+  generation 1); a **replayed** emit against a run holding events but no registry row — the
+  state the durable run is in today — registers it while still returning the original event;
+  an emit into an already-registered run preserves the generation a restore bumped; a refused
+  emit registers too; and an append that fails structural validation rolls the registration
+  back with it (never a phantom generation).
+  `tests/test_bump_generation_cli.py` gains the end-to-end case: a scratch run written only
+  through `omegahive emit` takes `bump-generation` (1 → 2). The two CLI fixtures now clear
+  their run's `runs` row as well as its events, since an emit writes both.
+- **Docs** — `docs/omegahive_recovery_runbook.md` §4 step 3 and the deployment-#0 record
+  (`docs/deployments/deployment-0-beastie.md`, Restore drill) drop the inert-bump caveat and
+  its "restore ⇒ restart every client, no exceptions" interim rule.
+
+Untouched, per the order's stop-lines: generation semantics, `GENERATION_MISMATCH` handling,
+cursor logic, and the schema (`open_run` was already in the store; nothing new is created).
+No generation was bumped on any run but the throwaway scratch one.
+
+**Workspace:**
+
+- `projects/omegahive/RUNBOOK.md` — restore step 3 loses the caveat and the one-time
+  out-of-band `open_run` wire-up block. Both halves of the invalidation step stay, and the
+  restart half now carries the reason it is permanent rather than interim (below).
+- this report.
+
+## How verified
+
+- **Suite:** `uv run pytest` — **409 passed** against a scratch Postgres database (created
+  for the run, dropped after; the durable store was never touched). `uv run ruff check .`
+  clean; `uv run mypy` clean, 181 source files.
+- **Scratch-run drill** — the order's evidence leg, run end-to-end through the CLI against a
+  throwaway database and run id (`run-registration-drill-<UTC>`), dropped afterwards. Its
+  middle section reproduces the durable run's actual state — events with no registry row —
+  and puts a replayed emit against it:
+
+  ```
+  --- runs registry before any emit ---
+  []
+  --- bump-generation BEFORE any emit (must refuse) ---
+  run not registered (no generation): 'run-registration-drill-20260813-224429'
+  exit=1
+  --- first emit through the CLI write path ---
+  emitted · goal.received · seq 1
+  --- runs registry after the first emit ---
+  [('run-registration-drill-20260813-224429', 1)]
+  --- second emit: registry untouched (no-op when present) ---
+  emitted · worker.registered · seq 2
+  rows: 1 · generation: 1 · events: 2
+  --- the live run's state: events, no registry row (row dropped by hand) ---
+  runs: 0 · events: 2
+  --- next emit is a REPLAY (identical content -> same derived key) ---
+  already recorded (idempotent) · worker.registered · seq 2
+  rows: 1 · generation: 1 · events: 2 (no new event, run registered)
+  --- bump-generation on the scratch run (must succeed) ---
+  generation bumped for 'run-registration-drill-20260813-224429': 1 -> 2
+  --- a stale cursor now gets GENERATION_MISMATCH ---
+  stale-cursor read -> generation_mismatch: True · generation: 2
+  full snapshot     -> generation_mismatch: False · adopts generation: 2
+  cursor read after snapshot -> generation_mismatch: False
+  ```
+
+  So: refuses before the run exists, registers on the first emit, no-ops on the second,
+  registers a run that already holds events even when the emit dedups to a replay, bumps, and
+  the bump reaches a live client as a mismatch it recovers from — the whole
+  restore-invalidation path, on a run that only `emit` ever wrote to.
+- **Not verified here — the live `omegahive` row.** It requires the merged image running on
+  the stack, which post-dates this result. The verification query is in **To operate**.
+
+## To operate
+
+1. **Which wire-up path the live run takes: item 1 of the order — the next real emit.** No
+   one-time command is needed. Once the PR is merged and the image rebuilt, the next emit on
+   the `omegahive` run (any board event — a launch, an answer, a close) opens the run as a
+   side effect, and the RUNBOOK's out-of-band `open_run` block is gone because nothing needs
+   it. Deploy is the ordinary close-time step for a service-touching task:
+
+   ```sh
+   cd ~/src/SNET/omegahive && git checkout main && git pull
+   podman compose build            # rebuild the omegahive image — the CLI is what changed
+   scripts/deploy_checks.sh
+   ```
+
+   Changed services: none run continuously off this code path except the **notifier**
+   (restart it with the rest of the stack as usual); the change lives in the `cli` one-shot
+   that `hive emit` / the wrappers invoke, so it takes effect on the next emit after the
+   rebuild.
+
+2. **Confirm the row, after the next emit:**
+
+   ```sh
+   podman compose --profile ops run --rm --entrypoint sh backup -c \
+     "psql \"\$OMEGAHIVE_DATABASE_URL\" -c \"SELECT * FROM runs WHERE run_id='omegahive'\""
+   ```
+
+   Expect one row at `generation = 1`. Until that row exists, the restore floor is still
+   "restart every client" — which you do anyway (point 4).
+
+3. **If you want the row before the next emit** (e.g. you are about to restore and there has
+   been no board activity since the rebuild), register it directly — one-time, reversible,
+   and *not* a generation bump:
+
+   ```sh
+   podman compose run --rm --entrypoint python cli -c \
+     "from omegahive.db import connect; from omegahive.port import open_run
+   c=connect(); open_run(c,'omegahive'); c.commit(); print('registered')"
+   # reverse with:  psql … -c "DELETE FROM runs WHERE run_id='omegahive'"
+   ```
+
+4. **Restore procedure: still do both halves of step 3.** The bump is no longer inert, but it
+   does not replace restarting every client. A restore rewinds the `runs` row along with the
+   log, so the bump that follows it can land on a generation some client has already seen —
+   restore a dump older than a previous restore's bump and the numbers collide. Both runbooks
+   now say this in place of the old interim wording.
+
+5. **A running notifier needs no restart to pick the token up.** `PortSpineReader` adopts any
+   non-`None` generation it reads, so the first poll after the run is registered seeds it at
+   1 and every later bump reaches it as a mismatch.
+
+6. **Never bump the live run to test this.** A live bump forces every client to re-snapshot
+   and nothing here needs it; the bump evidence above is from the scratch run only.
+
+7. **Open the PR.** The branch is `feature/run-registration` (four commits) in the code clone;
+   pushing and opening the PR is the operator's act, as is merging.
+
+## Reflection
+
+- **The open belongs ahead of every early exit, not just ahead of the accept branch.** The
+  order says "the emit path opens the run when absent", and `emit()` has three ways out that
+  each leave an event standing in the run: the accepted append, the refusal (which writes a
+  `gateway.rejected` feedback record, §5), and the idempotency early-return (which hands back
+  an event committed by an earlier call). Open only on accept, or only after the dedup check,
+  and a run whose next traffic is a refusal or a retry keeps holding events with no generation
+  token — the exact defect, one branch further in. The replay branch is the one that matters
+  most in practice, because it is what an at-least-once caller does and what the live run's
+  own wire-up emit is most likely to be. So the open is the first statement in the
+  transaction, and a test pins each branch.
+- **Placement is the gateway, not the store.** `EventLog.append()` is the dumber seam and
+  would have covered a few direct-append callers too, but "the emit path" in the order is the
+  governed one, and the gateway's `emit()` already owns the atomic per-run unit — the advisory
+  lock, the idempotency lookup, the commit boundary. Putting registration there gets "same
+  transaction as the event insert" for free and leaves the store's read/write helpers alone.
+  Direct `EventLog.append()` callers (a handful of store-level unit tests) stay unregistered;
+  nothing in production writes that way.
+- **The restart step is permanent, not interim — and the old wording hid that.** Both runbooks
+  framed "restart every client" as a stopgap that the generation token would retire. It never
+  could: `runs` lives in the same database as `events`, so a restore rewinds the generation
+  counter too, and the post-restore bump can reproduce a number a client already holds
+  (restoring a dump older than a previous restore's bump). Rare, but the failure mode is a
+  silent skipping read — the exact thing the token exists to prevent. I rewrote both to say
+  "do both, every time", with the reason. This is documentation only; the order's stop-line on
+  generation semantics is intact, and the collision is a property of the design, not of this
+  change.
+- **One doc outside the order's list.** The order names the two runbooks; the deployment-#0
+  record (`docs/deployments/deployment-0-beastie.md`) carried the same caveat as a standing
+  **Open item**, phrased as an operating rule ("restore ⇒ restart every client, no
+  exceptions"). Leaving it would have made the code repo contradict itself on the point this
+  task exists to settle, so I closed it there too — same three sentences, plus the row-check
+  query.
+- **Two legs of the definition of done are not mine to close.** The live `omegahive` row
+  needs the merged image on the stack and an emit after it — an operator act that post-dates
+  any worker's result, the same boundary the backups task recorded. And this report is not
+  announced on the spine: I have no emit wrapper in this environment. Both are named above so
+  nothing depends on remembering them.
+- **A dump older than the rebuild replays as an unregistered run.** Restore one and
+  `bump-generation` refuses again until the next emit re-registers the run — which resets the
+  generation to 1, below whatever clients last saw. The restart-every-client half covers it;
+  the RUNBOOK says so at the point of use. Not worth special-casing in code: it is a
+  one-window artifact of the changeover, and it argues for the restart floor rather than
+  against it.
